thread:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: Platform p95 latency breach detected for text-generation (region routing oscillation suspected). p95=1450ms across many routes, automatic routing switches observed. Paging sre_oncall and ml_oncall.

sre_oncall: I see the alert, logging in now. grabbing traces.

ml_oncall: Received. On it. Initial hypothesis: dynamic routing policy triggered fallback to lower-cost region/model, which then hot-edges and triggers reroute back -> loop.

alice.nguyen: Customers are reporting timeouts and 502s in US-EAST. Any immediate mitigation?

jonathan.k: Can we disable dynamic routing policy temporarily? That should stop flips.

ml_oncall: Yes, recommend: 1) set routing.policy.dynamic=false (temp) 2) pin model variant to a stable variant in us-east 3) spin up warm instances in secondary region.

ops_bot: Executing: `redwoodctl routing update --policy dynamic=false --scope org` by ops_bot. Result: OK.

sre_oncall: Applied static routing to prioritize us-east, rolling back dynamic decisions. Monitoring for stability.

maria_k: Noted surge in failed requests: 3.7% 5xx over 10m window, top error `context deadline exceeded` and `model_kv_miss`.

ml_oncall: Looking at model variants used: traffic was bouncing between `gpt-x-16k-singleq` (fast path) and `gpt-x-quant-v2` (smaller). The quant variant's cold-starts added 200-400ms and caused p95 to spike beyond the policy threshold, triggering reroute back. There's a feedback loop because routing uses p95 to evaluate region/model.

alice.nguyen: Can we pin to `gpt-x-16k-singleq` for the affected tenant groups while we warm quant instances?

ml_oncall: Doing per-tenant override: `redwoodctl traffic override --tenant pattern=prod_* --model gpt-x-16k-singleq --until 1768516400`

incident-bot: Audit: override applied by ml_oncall at 2026-03-15T02:05:12Z.

jonathan.k: Also adding a short cool-down so routing doesn't flip on transient spikes. Lower sensitivity = good.

maria_k: On-call note: created temporary dashboard to track routing flip-rate (`/dash/routing/flip_rate`) and p95 per-region.

product_lead: Heads-up: a handful of paying customers in finance cluster reported degraded tail latencies — CS is notifying them. Keep me posted about ETA for full recovery.

ml_oncall: Warmup script started to pre-load KV for quant variants in secondary region: `for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "x-api-key: REDACTED" https://api.redwood.dev/generate -d '{"prompt":"warm"}'; done`

ops_bot: Warmup job status: 200/200 completed in 8m. Latencies for quant instances improved to ~350ms median.

sre_oncall: Post-mitigation p95 dropped to ~720ms, flip-rate reduced from ~12/min to 0-1/min. Customer impact trending down.

maria_k: Quick impact estimate: ~2.8% of requests experienced >1s latency and ~0.6% hit 5xx during peak. Affected tenants: prod-alpha, prod-finance, partner-inference.

jonathan.k: Rolling back static pin? Or keep until next deploy window?

ml_oncall: Keep pin for 1 more hour to ensure KV caches are stable. We'll add feature flag to allow gradual re-enable with higher hysteresis.

incident-bot: SEV2 -> mitigation in place. Tracking continues.

alice.nguyen: I'm going to draft a customer-facing note for the affected tenants. cc @product_lead.

product_lead: TY. Please mention root cause: routing hysteresis + cold-start latency for quant variant. Include steps taken and ETA for re-enable.

ml_oncall: Follow-up actions (short):
- add metric: routing_flip_rate and an alert at 5/min
- add hysteresis to policy evaluation: require 3 consecutive p95 breaches before reroute
- add warmup probe for quant variants on scale-up

jonathan.k: Ops runbook edits: add `redwoodctl routing set --cooldown` example and a checklist for model-variant pinning.

sre_oncall: Preparing handoff to next_oncall in 30m. Current status: stable, p95 ~700-780ms, flip-rate 0-1/min. Will monitor for 1h post-handoff.

next_oncall: I got the handoff. Will keep watch and escalate if pattern returns.

incident-bot: Incident closed to active response at 2026-03-15T03:40:00Z. Follow-up required: postmortem and action items assigned.

maria_k: Filing postmortem ticket: `PM-1284` with RCA draft and timelines. Assigned to ml_oncall and jonathan.k for fixes.

alice.nguyen: Draft of customer note attached to PM-1284. Will send after final wording.

product_lead: Good work team. Let's ensure we have a playbook entry for SLO-driven routing oscillation. :thumbsup:

ml_oncall: Adding example config diff to the ticket: `- routing.p95_threshold: 800ms
+ routing.p95_threshold: 1200ms
+ routing.hysteresis.count: 3`

jonathan.k: Also propose a unit test for the routing evaluator to simulate back-and-forth metric noise.

incident-bot: Participants acknowledged. Thread archived when follow-ups created.
